Date: 2027-04-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Intermittent throughput surge impacting API calls (incident ID P-0417)

Neha / Redwood ops team,

We experienced a burst of 5xx errors and elevated latency across our production integration between 08:55 and 09:05 PT this morning. Traffic patterns show an unusually high token rate that appears to have caused timeouts and retries in our ingestion pipeline. Impact: some customers saw transaction failures (estimated 1.8% of calls) and increased latency up to ~3.5s for generation endpoints.

We opened an incident on our side and saw retries compounding the load. Can you confirm whether any autoscaling or routing changes were pushed on Redwood around that window? We need an accelerated RCA and a plan to prevent recurrence — Polaris execs are asking for an executive readout today if possible.

Attaching a short log excerpt and our correlation graphs.

Attachments: polaris_logs_excerpt_0417.txt (log snippet)

Alex Turner
Head of Integrations
Polaris Systems

Subject: Re: Intermittent throughput surge impacting API calls (incident ID P-0417)

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I'm very sorry Polaris hit this — we take these incidents seriously. We're triaging now. Initial notes:

- No scheduled deploys or config pushes from Redwood in that window.
- Our telemetry shows a short burst of high-concurrency prefix patterns that triggered fallback kernel paths and caused a localized autoscaler spike in the us-west region.
- Triage runbook is engaged (Marcus & Jonas on the runtime side; Laura on canary validation; Grace on customer comms).

I'll deliver a concise RCA draft by EOD PT and a mitigation plan with owner-level commitments first thing tomorrow. If Polaris leadership wants an exec readout today, we can carve out 30m at 4:30 PT — please let me know if that works.

Again — apologies. We're prioritizing containment and a durable fix.

Date: 2027-04-17T18:27:00Z
Subject: [Internal] Polaris incident P-0417 — RCA draft + actions (attached)

Team — internal RCA draft attached. Summary highlights:

1) What happened (summary)
- At ~08:56 PT there was a traffic burst from Polaris that increased concurrent prefix lengths and triggered the runtime to fall back to a conservative kernel and disable KV-prefix caching for that workload class.
- The fallback path caused per-token CPU increases and delayed KV hot-path responses; combined with a short autoscaler race condition we saw a transient capacity gap. Retries from Polaris' client SDK amplified the burst.

2) Root causes (multiple)
- Runtime: conservative kernel selection for rare prefix shapes (TICKET: RUNTIME-582).
- Orchestration: autoscaler decision race under sudden concurrency transient (TICKET: ORCH-343).
- Caching: KV prefix eviction threshold was too aggressive for the observed burst profile (TICKET: CACHE-129).

3) Immediate mitigations performed
- Increased autoscaler target floor for Polaris tenant in us-west for next 24h. (deployed at 10:15 PT)
- Re-enabled a non-conservative kernel path for matched prefix hashes as hotfix (rolled at 11:05 PT).

4) Proposed permanent actions and owners (deadline in parentheses)
- Marcus: hotfix formalization + regression test (Marcus Lin) (2027-04-22)
- Laura: canary plan and load validation with Polaris traffic samples (Laura Bennett) (2027-04-20)
- Jonas: autoscaler race mitigation + rollout strategy (Jonas Weber) (2027-04-21)
- Grace: customer communications & weekly progress notes (Grace O'Connor) (ongoing)

Attachments: polaris_throughput_rca_20270417.pdf

Please review and flag gaps. I want explicit owner signoff by tomorrow morning so we can present a committed timeline to Polaris.

Thanks,
Neha
